Meta-analysis physiological costs of hibernation: Report 7 - OS Aestivation

Pablo Capilla-Lasheras

2026-05-06

This R Markdown Notebook contains the initial meta-analysis for the project ‘physiological ’costs’ of hibernation. Specifically, the meta-analysis of hibernation

Dataset and calculation of effect sizes

The dataset for this meta-analysis has been collected from the literature and curated by Pablo Burraco, Marko Prokic and Tamara Petrovic. It contains data on physiological effects of hibernation in different systems. Here a quick snapshot of the first lines of the dataset:

# dataset with raw data
data <- openxlsx::read.xlsx(
  here(
    "./01_data/raw_data/Burraco_et_al_estivation_hibernation.xlsx"
  ),
  colNames = T,
  sheet = 1
)

paged_table(data, options = list(rows.print = 20))

As a summary of the initial dataset:

  • Number of studies: 20
  • Number of species: 12

For this initial meta-analysis, I am going to include all oxidative stress (OS) markers and calculate the standarised mean difference (g; with heteroscedastic population variances) as the effect size of analysis comparing aestivation versus euthermia. Positive SMD values indicate higher OS values in aestivation while negative SMD indicate lower OS values in aestivation. This is a summary of the effect size calculation based on the dataset above:

# ES data
# note that there is a very large effect size (~40), we have checked this effect size and the raw data and the data as collected is correct
data <- readRDS(
  here(
    "./01_data/processed_RDS_data_files/07_OS_metaanalysis_aestivation_full_data.RDS"
  )
)
data$obsID <- 1:nrow(data) # observation ID

# handling species names for phylogenetic-controlled models
data$Species <- replace_values(
  data$Species,
  "Ranoidea alboguttata" ~ "Cyclorana alboguttata" # correcting synomyn names manuallty
)

data$scientific_name <- gsub(
  x = data$Species,
  pattern = "_",
  replacement = " "
)

data$scientific_name_phylo <- data$scientific_name

## data for SMD
df_SMD <- data %>%
  filter(!is.na(SMDH)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(SMDH.sv))

# matrix with phylogentic correlations
phylo_cor <- readRDS(
  here(
    "./01_data/processed_RDS_data_files/07_OS_phylogenetic_correlations_aestivation.RDS"
  )
)

phylo_tree <- readRDS(
  here(
    "./01_data/processed_RDS_data_files/07_OS_phylogenetic_tree_aestivation.RDS"
  )
)

tree <- ggtree(phylo_tree, size = 1.2) +
  xlim_tree(c(0, 35)) +
  geom_tiplab(
    aes(
      label = paste0(
        "italic('",
        sub(x = label, pattern = "_", replacement = " "),
        "')"
      )
    ),
    parse = TRUE,
    offset = 0.5,
    size = 5,
    hjust = 0
  )

ggsave(
  filename = here(
    "./03_plots/03_aestivation/00a_OS_phylo_tree.png"
  ),
  plot = tree,
  device = "png",
  height = 150,
  width = 90,
  units = "mm"
)

ggsave(
  filename = here(
    "./03_plots/03_aestivation/00a_OS_phylo_tree.pdf"
  ),
  plot = tree,
  height = 150,
  width = 90,
  units = "mm"
)

Summary of SMD effect size and number of observations included in the meta-analysis:

summary(df_SMD$SMDH)
##    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
## -6.3124 -0.6132  0.1880  0.3318  1.0275 43.9933
print(tree)

  • Number of observation with non-missing SMD: 346
  • Number of studies in the dataset for analysis: 19
  • Number of species in the dataset for analysis: 11

Initial meta-analysis:

This initial model contains only the intercept and four random effects to account for phylogenetic variation and variation between and within studies beyond sampling variance.

## calculate var-cover matrix to control for correlated effect sizes within study and tissue
V <- vcalc(
  vi = SMDH.sv,
  cluster = StudyID,
  subgroup = Tissue,
  grp1 = Hib_M,
  grp2 = Euthermia_M,
  w1 = Hib_N,
  w2 = Euthermia_N,
  data = df_SMD
)

# model
model_SMD <- rma.mv(
  yi = SMDH,
  V = V,
  mods = ~1,
  random = list(
    ~ 1 | scientific_name_phylo,
    ~ 1 | Species,
    ~ 1 | obsID,
    ~ 1 | StudyID
  ),
  data = df_SMD,
  R = list(scientific_name_phylo = phylo_cor),
  method = "REML",
  control = list(optimizer = "BFGS"),
  verbose = F
)
saveRDS(
  object = model_SMD,
  file = here(
    './04_models/03_aestivation/01a_metamodel_aestivation_OS.RDS'
  )
)
model_SMD <- readRDS(
  file = here(
    './04_models/03_aestivation/01a_metamodel_aestivation_OS.RDS'
  )
)
summary(model_SMD)
## 
## Multivariate Meta-Analysis Model (k = 340; method: REML)
## 
##    logLik   Deviance        AIC        BIC       AICc   
## -579.8381  1159.6763  1169.6763  1188.8063  1169.8565   
## 
## Variance Components:
## 
##             estim    sqrt  nlvls  fixed                 factor    R 
## sigma^2.1  0.0001  0.0121     11     no  scientific_name_phylo  yes 
## sigma^2.2  0.0187  0.1366     11     no                Species   no 
## sigma^2.3  0.6658  0.8160    340     no                  obsID   no 
## sigma^2.4  0.2214  0.4705     19     no                StudyID   no 
## 
## Test for Heterogeneity:
## Q(df = 339) = 940.3509, p-val < .0001
## 
## Model Results:
## 
## estimate      se    zval    pval    ci.lb   ci.ub    
##   0.1792  0.1390  1.2887  0.1975  -0.0933  0.4517    
## 
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
i2_SMD <- round(i2_ml(model_SMD), digits = 4) # heterogeneity random effects

Proportion of variation left after accounting for sampling variance and proportion accounted by each random effect:

knitr::kable(
  x = data.frame(
    Variable = names(i2_SMD),
    i2_value_percentage = as.numeric(round(i2_SMD, digits = 3))
  )
) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = F)

Plot of results of intercept-only model:

overall_plot <- orchard_plot(

Publication bias: small-study effects

df_SMD$inv_eff_ss <- (1 / df_SMD$Hib_N) + (1 / df_SMD$Euthermia_N)

model_SMD_pb <- rma.mv(
  yi = SMDH,
  V = V,
  mods = ~ 1 + sqrt(inv_eff_ss),
  random = list(
    ~ 1 | scientific_name_phylo,
    ~ 1 | Species,
    ~ 1 | obsID,
    ~ 1 | StudyID
  ),
  data = df_SMD,
  R = list(scientific_name_phylo = phylo_cor),
  method = "REML",
  control = list(optimizer = "BFGS"),
  verbose = F
)
saveRDS(
  object = model_SMD_pb,
  file = here(
    './04_models/03_aestivation/06a_pb_metamodel_aestivation_OS.RDS'
  )
)
model_SMD_pb <- readRDS(
  file = here(
    './04_models/03_aestivation/06a_pb_metamodel_aestivation_OS.RDS'
  )
)

summary(model_SMD_pb)

Publication bias: time-lag effects

df_SMD$year_scl <- scale(df_SMD$Year)

model_SMD_tl <- rma.mv(
  yi = SMDH,
  V = V,
  mods = ~ 1 + year_scl,
  random = list(
    ~ 1 | scientific_name_phylo,
    ~ 1 | Species,
    ~ 1 | obsID,
    ~ 1 | StudyID
  ),
  data = df_SMD,
  R = list(scientific_name_phylo = phylo_cor),
  method = "REML",
  control = list(optimizer = "BFGS"),
  verbose = F
)
saveRDS(
  object = model_SMD_tl,
  file = here(
    './04_models/03_aestivation/07a_timelag_metamodel_aestivation_OS.RDS'
  )
)
model_SMD_tl <- readRDS(
  file = here(
    './04_models/03_aestivation/07a_timelag_metamodel_aestivation_OS.RDS'
  )
)

summary(model_SMD_tl)

The results above suggest some degree of time-lag bias.

results <- mod_results(model_SMD_tl, mod = "year_scl", group = "StudyID")
time_bias <- orchaRd::bubble_plot(
  model_SMD_tl,
  mod = 'year_scl',
  group = 'StudyID',
  alpha = 0.2,
  cb = FALSE,
  xlab = "Year of publication (scaled)",
  transfm = "none",
) +
  theme(
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12, angle = 0),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 16)
  )

ggsave(
  filename = here(
    "./03_plots/03_aestivation/06a_overall_plot_aestivation_OS.png"
  ),
  device = 'png',
  plot = time_bias,
  height = 110,
  width = 185,
  units = "mm"
)
ggsave(

)

Meta-analysis with all organisms but including different OS markers:
